text:
CNN host questions Trump's health issues(Image: CNN)

President Donald Trump’s latest annual medical check-up is making headlines after reports revealed it involved consultations with 22 specialists.

This amount of doctors is nearly double the number from his 2019 exam and more than any previous presidential record. According to reports, Trump's figure surpasses former President George W. Bush’s record by 10 specialists. The group included physicians from Harvard, Duke and other leading institutions, along with general practitioners.

The unusually large number has sparked some concern. Some medical experts described the scale of the evaluation as “extraordinary,” raising questions about why such an extensive team was necessary for a sitting U.S. president. This comes just after the president sparked similar fears following an on-air blunder.

The issue gained more attention during a recent CNN segment, when host Jake Tapper spoke with Dr. Jonathan Reiner about the president’s condition. Referencing visible concerns, Tapper asked, “What kinds of specialists would typically be included in this assessment? As we’re seeing right now, a big bruise on the president’s hand. We are seeing these health issues.”

Dr. Reiner explained that when presidents face specific medical concerns, specialists are typically brought in to address those individual issues, rather than relying solely on general evaluations. He also added that there is "no sense" in the note Trump provided from his own physician.

Viewers chimed in online, with one saying, “And nobody can figure out why he’s so f--king stupid.” Another added on X, “The first 21 refused to give him a clean bill of health?”

Despite the speculation, the White House has maintained that the expanded medical team reflects best practices for executive care. Trump’s physician, Dr. Sean Barbabella, stated that the president remains in excellent health, citing strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall function.

However, some doctors have pointed to gaps in the publicly released report. Missing details, including results from a cardiovascular ultrasound, have led to additional questions. Others noted changes in Trump’s medication, including the apparent discontinuation of a hair loss drug.

The renewed scrutiny comes after years of concern over the president’s age. At 79, Trump is already one of the oldest individuals to hold the office.

Trump was found with bruises on his hands(Image: CNN)

The medical exam comes after an unusual mid-year screening conducted in October and coincides with a series of viral moments. These include footage showing Trump walking in a “zigzag” pattern and claims that he appeared to fall asleep during the NBA Finals and other major events.

While no doctor has publicly diagnosed him with a neurological condition, the White House has confirmed that Trump has chronic venous insufficiency.

There have long been similar debates surrounding Joe Biden’s health during the 2024 campaign, suggesting that concerns about age and fitness remain a key issue for voters. He held office at 82-years-old.

Recent surveys show that 59% of respondents doubt Trump’s mental acuity, while 55% question his physical health. Observers note that these results could have an impact on his political standing moving forward.
